question.text: If the ICAI-SIAB debars an empanelled SIA from accepting new assurance engagements for a period of three years, revocation or early restoration of the empanelment can typically be sought on which of the following grounds?

answer.text: A successful appeal to the appellate authority or a subsequent order of review by SIAB on new material facts / compliance with conditions imposed.
Mere passage of one year - the SIA is automatically restored after one year.
Payment of a token fee of INR 10,000 to SIAB.
Registration as an SIA with any other SRO.

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Restoration / revocation of a debarment order typically requires either: (i) a successful appeal to the designated appellate authority that sets aside or modifies the debarment, or (ii) a review order by SIAB itself upon the SIA demonstrating compliance with conditions imposed and/or new material facts not previously considered. Automatic time-based restoration and nominal-fee release are not default mechanisms. **The Trap:** Automatic restoration / fee-based release / registration with a parallel SRO are all inconsistent with a quasi-judicial disciplinary order that remains in force till set aside. **Cross-Exam Context:** III-A/III-C tests SEBI order revocation architecture; XXIII imports the same to SIAB. **Assessor's Pro-Tip:** Track the debarment end-date plus a 30-day buffer. Thirty days before the expiry, file an undertaking-of-compliance package with SIAB so that the empanelment is restored without a fresh application cycle.
